checks.evidence: Three separate, color-coded rows identify A, B and C with signed scores −1.0, +0.7 and +1.3.
Each score row aligns with a matching-color, right-extending bar labeled with its exponential. All bars have positive length, ordered A < B < C; row position and color connect each input to its mass.

Three mass bars appear above one total, Σ = 6.051. However, the three small colored arrows sit beneath C's bar without visible connections from A and B. The bars are neither joined nor stacked into a total, so the geometry only weakly supports all three contributing.

One horizontal capacity is completely tiled by adjacent cyan, purple and orange segments labeled 0.061, 0.333 and 0.606. Their relative widths match the mass-bar proportions, supporting the caption that probabilities add to 1.

videos.reconstructed_message: Convert three signed class scores into positive exponential masses, sum those masses, then divide each by that same total so their shares fill one probability budget.
videos.limits: At 11s, division is stated in text but no geometric rescaling into probabilities is visible. At 14s and 17s, the finished partition is visible. English explanations and small denominator text limit accessibility for a Chinese newcomer.

Each input row aligns with its exponential label and matching-color positive-length bar. The common bar baseline and increasing lengths A < B < C make the input-to-mass correspondence visible.

All three exponential bars remain individually labeled above one explicit sum. Small colored arrow marks converge beneath C's bar, but their paths from the three separate bars are not visible. The written addition is clearer than the geometric demonstration of contribution.

Three matching-color segments adjoin without gaps inside a single horizontal span beneath P(A) + P(B) + P(C) = 1. Their widths correspond to the mass ratios, and class labels identify the shares as 0.061, 0.333 and 0.606.

videos.reconstructed_message: Each class produces a positive exponential mass; all masses enter one sum, and each class takes its own mass divided by that sum, yielding three shares of one whole.
videos.limits: At 11s, division is described rather than geometrically demonstrated. Persistent exponential labels at 8s, 14s and 17s help identify the bars, but explanations remain English and several labels are small.

comparisons.reason: Y has a modest component-identity advantage: at 8s and 14s, exponential labels remain beside the corresponding colored bars, whereas Z drops them. Both show proportional masses and a contiguous final partition at 14s, but neither clearly connects all three masses to the shared total at 8s or geometrically demonstrates division at 11s. No visible mathematical contradiction distinguishes them. Y's advantage comes from persistent correspondence, not additional text; both have small English labels that constrain newcomer readability.

response.uncertainty: Assessment covers only supplied frames at 1, 4, 8, 11, 14 and 17 seconds. Unseen transitions, narration, actual learning, production methods and checks cannot be assessed. Both support how a shared total produces one whole, but the causal aggregation step remains visually uncertain.
